subject: USER TRANSCRIPT: a durable, user-facing record of what a student actually did on Hexworth Prime
description:
Scoped 2026-08-08 in ~/hexworth-shared/User-History/. Today the platform holds a student's history scattered across ~14 Firestore collections (progress, quiz_attempts, challenge_attempts, flag_captures, submissions, score_submissions, class_progress, enrollments, tool_invocations, sextant_runs, edt/pfi submissions, users/*) with NO single per-user view and no canonical shape. Trial Run consumes item.attempt/item.complete as Tier A evidence, which means an unspecified, undocumented data contract is already load-bearing for a product that tells people what their record supports. CONSTRAINT FOUND IN SEARCH: Dr Hex conversation memory deliberately has NO transcript export and a 30-min lifetime (_docs/architecture/hex-ai-conversation-memory-design.md:194) -- AI chat is NOT a transcript source, by prior decision. CONSTRAINT 2: the Observatory consent draft promises research data is deleted on withdrawal and 'cannot be recovered or returned to you' (_docs/research/observatory-consent-amendment-draft-2026-06-22.md), and carries an open [PI TO CONFIRM] on whether any export survives deletion -- a transcript feature is exactly such an export, so the boundary between platform record and research record must be explicit BEFORE build. See User-History/01-user-transcript-scope.md
[2026-08-08 21:36] SCOPE CORRECTED 2026-08-08 by operator: 'transcript' means a COLLEGE TRANSCRIPT -- completed courses and proven skills -- not an activity log. Re-measured against that. HEADLINE: proven skills is CLOSER TO BUILDABLE than completed courses, the opposite of what you would expect. COURSES: no registry, no server-side completion fact, no grade at all (gradebook/finalGrade/letterGrade/gpa = ZERO hits across the tree); CourseProgress.js is localStorage-only and loaded by 1 page. Keiser Master Syllabi (75+, real codes CGS1000C/CIS2253/COP1034C) exist as .docx source, not a platform registry. SKILLS: _app/lab-skill-maps/*.yaml (34 files) already declare primary+secondary skill, layer (Execution/Recognition), an evidence_required rule saying what counts as PROOF, and an assessed_artifact. 26 of 34 assess by FLAG, and flags land server-side in users/{uid}/flag_captures (functions/ctf-stats.js:50). So skill attainment is ALREADY PROVABLE for ~26 labs with no new telemetry. Coverage is the limit: 34 maps vs 810 labs (4%). The skill maps were built to gate Dr Hex help levels and happen to be exactly the right shape for an attainment record. Rewritten scope: User-History/01-user-transcript-scope.md
[2026-08-08 21:58] PART B ANCHORING SCOPED 2026-08-08 (User-History/03-skill-anchoring-and-badges.md), from operator brainstorm 'how about badges'. VERDICT: badges are the right WRAPPER, wrong ANCHOR -- a badge is a claim engineered to travel WITHOUT its evidence, which is exactly what Trial Run exists to catch. Hard rule: a badge is NON-DETACHABLE from its evidence and its layer. THE ANCHOR IS TWO AXES: (1) WHAT = MITRE ATT&CK technique id / cert objective, external + machine-validatable, 316 technique ids already in _app but only 26 labs; (2) HOW DEEP = the FOUR-LAYER cognitive model ALREADY IN PRODUCTION at dr-hex-lab-skill-map.md:60-63 -- Recognition / Hypothesis / Execution / Transfer, measured distribution 27/21/14/3 across the 34 maps. Axis 2 is the anti-overclaim mechanism and it is the half badges normally lack: 'Recognition of T1003.001' vs 'Execution of T1003.001' are different claims and both are honest; 'Credential Access' is neither. NICE work roles proposed as ROLL-UP (career-outcome legible), not as the atom. HARD COVERAGE NUMBER: 810 labs, 34 skill maps, 26 flag-proven, 26 with technique ids, and only TWO labs have BOTH. Model is sound, nearly everything is unbuilt; the real project is coverage authoring, not taxonomy. Fix now because expensive later: stamp-at-earning with versions, expiry, coarse badges + fine evidence, never award a layer the lab did not assess, hard separation from the XP/achievement economy (BUG-073 sprawl precedent).
